# Verify and explain your results

Choose a retained source variant. Replace `YOUR_VARIANT_ID`:

```bash
python scripts/python/verify_variant.py data/my-study results/my-study YOUR_VARIANT_ID
```

## Check more than a small p-value

- Verify the source allele pair and effect units.
- Recalculate beta/SE, the nominal interval and source −log10(p).
- Compare the derived normal Wald strength with the source test definition.
- Trace one excluded record to its source and filter reason.
- Reconcile one count and one plotted value with saved evidence.

The verifier checks a retained row. If a variant was excluded, inspect the QC table and preparation audit; do not alter the saved filter flag to make it appear in results.

## Write a defensible observation

“Variant [ID] had beta [value] per [effect allele] relative to [other allele] on [units], with source p [exact value]. The derived nominal interval was [lower, upper]. [State the relevant source-method or selection limitation.]”

Do not equate positive beta with harm, the nearest gene with the causal gene, or multiple nearby small-p rows with independent discoveries. A source-versus-Wald discrepancy can reflect different tests or correction; investigate before calling it an error.

## Plan the next check

Choose a next step that addresses a specific uncertainty: source harmonization review, build-matched annotation, matched LD, replication, a properly specified meta-analysis or another justified method. Explain what it would add. Do not ask AI to invent unavailable evidence.
